notes.front: What is construction work, as defined in section 1926.32?
notes.back: Work for construction, alteration and/or repair, including painting and decorating.
notes.explanation: This is the working definition used in Part 1926’s general definitions section.
notes.example: Like repainting a finished school during the holidays: it counts even though nothing new is being built.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.32(g), p. 25
notes.evidence: Construction work. For purposes of this section, Construction work means work for construction, alteration, and/

notes.front: What is a competent person under Part 1926?
notes.back: One capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards, who is authorised to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.
notes.explanation: Both parts are needed: the ability to spot hazards and the authority to act on them.
notes.example: Like a site foreman who can see that a stack of blocks is about to topple and has the power to stop work and restack it.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.32(f), p. 25
notes.evidence: Competent person means one who is capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards in the surroundings or working conditions which are unsanitary, hazardous, or dangerous to employees, and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.

notes.front: What is a qualified person under Part 1926?
notes.back: One who, by a recognised degree, certificate or professional standing, or extensive knowledge, training and experience, has shown ability to solve problems in the subject.
notes.explanation: The definition rests on demonstrated problem-solving ability; unlike a competent person, it says nothing about authority to act.
notes.example: Like a chartered structural engineer asked to design a temporary support, whether or not she runs the site.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.32(m), p. 26
notes.evidence: Qualified means one who, by possession of a recognized degree, certificate, or professional standing, or who by extensive knowledge, training, and experience, has successfully demonstrated his ability to solve or resolve problems relating to the subject matter, the work, or the project.

notes.front: What is an emergency action plan under section 1926.35?
notes.back: A plan, in writing save one exception, covering the actions employers and employees must take to keep employees safe from fire and other emergencies.
notes.explanation: Section 1926.35 applies to every emergency action plan that a particular OSHA standard requires.
notes.example: Like a building’s fire drill sheet, naming escape routes and who counts heads at the assembly point.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.35(a), p. 26
notes.evidence: The emergency action plan shall be in writing (except as provided in the last sentence of paragraph (e)(3) of this section) and shall cover those designated actions employers and employees must take to ensure employee safety from fire and other emergencies.

notes.front: By contracting for full performance of a contract, which employer obligations does the prime contractor assume?
notes.back: All of those prescribed under Part 1926, whether or not it subcontracts any of the work.
notes.explanation: Subcontracting passes on work, not the prime contractor’s responsibility for the whole contract.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.16(b), p. 23
notes.evidence: the prime contractor assumes all obligations prescribed as employer obligations under the standards contained in this part, whether or not he subcontracts any part of the work

notes.front: For subcontracted work, how is responsibility shared between the prime contractor and the subcontractor?
notes.back: They have joint responsibility; both are subject to the Act’s enforcement provisions.
notes.explanation: The subcontractor takes responsibility for its portion while the prime keeps the entire responsibility, so both answer for the same work.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.16(c), p. 23
notes.evidence: With respect to subcontracted work, the prime contractor and any subcontractor or subcontractors shall be deemed to have joint responsibility.

notes.front: If the prime contractor agrees to provide all first-aid and toilet facilities for its subcontractors, what responsibility do the subcontractors keep?
notes.back: Their legal responsibility; only the actual responsibility passes to the prime contractor.
notes.explanation: Part 1926 lets contractors share jobsite obligations by agreement, but the legal duty stays.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.16(a), p. 22
notes.evidence: thus relieving the subcontractors from the actual, but not any legal, responsibility

notes.front: If a specific standard and a general standard both apply to the same condition, which prevails?
notes.back: The specific standard.
notes.explanation: Part 1926 says a particular standard prevails over any different general standard for the same condition or practice.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.20(d)(1), p. 23
notes.evidence: If a particular standard is specifically applicable to a condition, practice, means, method, operation, or process, it shall prevail over any different general standard

notes.front: Whose responsibility is it to initiate and maintain the accident prevention programmes needed to comply with Part 1926?
notes.back: The employer’s.
notes.explanation: Section 1926.20(b) places the duty on the employer, and the programmes must include regular site inspections.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.20(b)(1), p. 23
notes.evidence: It shall be the responsibility of the employer to initiate and maintain such programs as may be necessary to comply with this part.

notes.front: Under section 1926.20(b)(2), who makes the frequent and regular inspections of job sites, materials and equipment?
notes.back: Competent persons designated by the employer.
notes.explanation: The inspections are part of the employer’s accident prevention programme.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.20(b)(2), p. 23
notes.evidence: Such programs shall provide for frequent and regular inspections of the job sites, materials, and equipment to be made by competent persons designated by the employers.

notes.front: What two options does Part 1926 give for a machine or tool that does not comply with the standards?
notes.back: Identify it as unsafe by tagging or locking its controls to make it inoperable; or physically remove it from its place of operation.
notes.explanation: Using non-compliant machinery, tools, materials or equipment is prohibited outright.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.20(b)(3), p. 23
notes.evidence: Such machine, tool, material, or equipment shall either be identified as unsafe by tagging or locking the controls to render them inoperable or shall be physically removed from its place of operation.

notes.front: Whom may an employer permit to operate equipment and machinery?
notes.back: Only employees qualified by training or experience.
notes.explanation: Section 1926.20(b)(4) places this limit on the employer.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.20(b)(4), p. 23
notes.evidence: The employer shall permit only those employees qualified by training or experience to operate equipment and machinery.

notes.front: What must the employer instruct each employee in, under section 1926.21(b)(2)?
notes.back: Recognising and avoiding unsafe conditions, and the regulations applicable to the work environment.
notes.explanation: The aim stated is to control or eliminate hazards or other exposure to illness or injury.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.21(b)(2), p. 24
notes.evidence: The employer shall instruct each employee in the recognition and avoidance of unsafe conditions and the regulations applicable to his work environment to control or eliminate any hazards or other exposure to illness or injury.

notes.front: Which employees must receive instruction on safe handling and use under section 1926.21(b)(3)?
notes.back: Those required to handle or use poisons, caustics and other harmful substances.
notes.explanation: This adds substance-specific instruction to the general duty to train every employee.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.21(b)(3), p. 24
notes.evidence: Employees required to handle or use poisons, caustics, and other harmful substances shall be instructed regarding the safe handling and use

notes.front: During construction, where must form and scrap lumber with protruding nails and other debris be kept cleared from?
notes.back: Work areas, passageways and stairs, in and around buildings or other structures.
notes.explanation: Section 1926.25 also requires combustible scrap to be removed at regular intervals.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.25(a), p. 24
notes.evidence: form and scrap lumber with protruding nails, and all other debris, shall be kept cleared from work areas, passageways, and stairs, in and around buildings or other structures

notes.front: When must provision be made for prompt medical attention in case of serious injury?
notes.back: Before the project begins.
notes.explanation: The employer must also ensure medical personnel are available for advice on occupational health.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.50(b), p. 27
notes.evidence: Provisions shall be made prior to commencement of the project for prompt medical attention in case of serious injury.

notes.front: When must a person with valid first-aid training be available at the worksite?
notes.back: When no infirmary, clinic, hospital or physician is reasonably accessible in time and distance for treating injured employees.
notes.explanation: The training can be from the U.S. Bureau of Mines, the American Red Cross, or equivalent training verified by documents.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.50(c), p. 27
notes.evidence: In the absence of an infirmary, clinic, hospital, or physician, that is reasonably accessible in terms of time and distance to the worksite

notes.front: How often must the employer check the first aid kit on each job?
notes.back: Before it is sent out on each job, and at least weekly on each job.
notes.explanation: The checks are to ensure that used items are replaced; the kit must be weatherproof with individually sealed items.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.50(d)(2), p. 27
notes.evidence: shall be checked by the employer before being sent out on each job and at least weekly on each job to ensure that the expended items are replaced

notes.front: What does section 1926.51 require about drinking water on site?
notes.back: An adequate supply of potable water; containers tightly closable with a tap; the common drinking cup is prohibited.
notes.explanation: Water must not be dipped from containers either.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.51(a), p. 28
notes.evidence: An adequate supply of potable water shall be provided in all places of employment. (2) Portable containers used to dispense drinking water shall be capable of being tightly closed, and equipped with a tap.

notes.front: Under temporary field conditions, what is the minimum toilet provision?
notes.back: Not less than one toilet facility must be available.
notes.explanation: Table D–1 otherwise sets the number of facilities by the number of employees.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.51(c)(2), p. 29
notes.evidence: Under temporary field conditions, provisions shall be made to assure not less than one toilet facility is available.

notes.front: When must construction areas, ramps, runways, corridors, offices, shops and storage areas be lit to the minimum intensities in Table D–3?
notes.back: While any work is in progress.
notes.explanation: The table gives minimum intensities in foot-candles by area or operation.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.56(a), p. 44
notes.evidence: shall be lighted to not less than the minimum illumination intensities listed in Table D– 3 while any work is in progress

notes.front: What are two of the minimum elements of an emergency action plan?
notes.back: Any two of, among others: escape procedures and route assignments; accounting for all employees after evacuation; rescue and medical duties.
notes.explanation: Section 1926.35 lists six minimum elements, including the preferred means of reporting fires and whom to contact.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.35(b), p. 27
notes.evidence: (1) Emergency escape procedures and emergency escape route assignments; (2) Procedures to be followed by employees who remain to operate critical plant operations before they evacuate; (3) Procedures to account for all employees after emergency evacuation has been completed; (4) Rescue and medical duties for those employees who are to perform them

notes.front: A general contractor subcontracts all steel erection. An inspector finds the steel crew without required protection. Who carries responsibility for that work under Part 1926?
notes.back: C: both the prime contractor and the subcontractor, jointly.
notes.choices:
A) Only the steel subcontractor
B) Only the prime contractor
C) Both the prime contractor and the subcontractor, jointly
D) Neither, until the owner accepts the work
notes.choicesExplained: A ignores the prime’s retained responsibility. B ignores the subcontractor’s responsibility for its part. D: nothing in Part 1926 waits on the owner.
notes.explanation: Where joint responsibility exists, both are subject to the enforcement provisions of the Act.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.16(d), p. 23
notes.evidence: Where joint responsibility exists, both the prime contractor and his subcontractor or subcontractors, regardless of tier, shall be considered subject to the enforcement provisions of the Act.

notes.front: A foreman finds a saw with a broken guard. He needs it for later but must not let it be used. What does Part 1926 allow?
notes.back: C: tag or lock its controls to make it inoperable, or remove it.
notes.choices:
A) Leave it with a verbal warning
B) Let only experienced workers use it
C) Tag or lock its controls to make it inoperable, or remove it
D) Use it until the end of the week
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and D all allow a non-compliant tool to stay usable, which Part 1926 prohibits.
notes.explanation: These are the two options Part 1926 gives for any non-compliant machine, tool, material or equipment.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.20(b)(3), p. 23
notes.evidence: The use of any machinery, tool, material, or equipment which is not in compliance with any applicable requirement of this part is prohibited.

notes.front: A site supervisor can spot a developing hazard in a trench and has the authority to stop work and fix it. Which Part 1926 role does he fit?
notes.back: A: competent person.
notes.choices:
A) Competent person
B) Qualified person, because he has authority
C) Neither, unless he holds a degree
D) Compliance Safety and Health Officer
notes.choicesExplained: B: the qualified-person definition turns on demonstrated problem-solving ability, not authority. C: no degree is needed for a competent person. D: that is an OSHA inspector.
notes.explanation: Recognising hazards plus authority for prompt corrective measures is the competent-person test.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.32(f), p. 25
notes.evidence: capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards in the surroundings or working conditions which are unsanitary, hazardous, or dangerous to employees, and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them

notes.front: A pipeline crew works two hours’ drive from the nearest clinic or hospital. What must the employer arrange?
notes.back: C: a person with valid first-aid training available at the worksite.
notes.choices:
A) Nothing, if workers carry mobile phones
B) A physician on site full time
C) A person with valid first-aid training available at the worksite
D) An infirmary built on site
notes.choicesExplained: A: phones alone do not meet the first-aid rule. B and D go beyond what section 1926.50 requires when no facility is reasonably accessible.
notes.explanation: The employer must also plan for prompt medical attention and transport or communication for an ambulance.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.50(c), p. 27
notes.evidence: Red Cross, or equivalent training that can be verified by documentary evidence, shall be available at the worksite to render first aid

notes.front: Stripped formwork with nails sticking out is piled across the stairway to the second floor. What does Part 1926 require?
notes.back: C: keep it cleared from stairs and passageways.
notes.choices:
A) Only a warning sign
B) Nothing until the end of the job
C) Keep it cleared from stairs and passageways
D) Remove it only if it is combustible
notes.choicesExplained: B: the duty applies during construction. A: a sign does not clear debris. D: all such debris must be cleared from these areas; combustibility only adds the regular-removal rule.
notes.explanation: Section 1926.25 names form and scrap lumber with protruding nails expressly.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.25(a), p. 24
notes.evidence: form and scrap lumber with protruding nails, and all other debris, shall be kept cleared from work areas, passageways, and stairs

notes.front: A new labourer is sent straight to work without being told about the site’s hazards or the rules for his job. Which duty has the employer missed?
notes.back: C: the duty to instruct each employee to recognise and avoid unsafe conditions.
notes.choices:
A) The general duty to post the OSHA notice
B) The duty to keep an OSHA 300 Log
C) The duty to instruct each employee to recognise and avoid unsafe conditions
D) The prime contractor’s duty to inspect
notes.choicesExplained: A and B are real duties but not about instruction. D concerns site inspections, not training each employee.
notes.explanation: Section 1926.21(b)(2) covers both hazards and the regulations that apply to the employee’s work environment.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.21(b)(2), p. 24
notes.evidence: The employer shall instruct each employee in the recognition and avoidance of unsafe conditions

notes.front: How does a competent person differ from a qualified person under Part 1926?
notes.back: A competent person spots hazards and is authorised to correct them; a qualified person has proven, by degree, certificate or experience, ability to solve problems.
notes.explanation: One definition centres on authority to act on hazards, the other on proven expertise.
notes.source: 29 CFR Part 1926 (revised as of 1 July 2025), § 1926.32(m), p. 26
notes.evidence: has successfully demonstrated his ability to solve or resolve problems relating to the subject matter, the work, or the project
